newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand share market closes at new high.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand share market closes at new high.

text.p: * NZ shares surges to new high despite higher interest rates
* Telecom leads the charge, but eases off all-time high
* Foreign buying seen in anticipation of further easing
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +28.35 at 2,570.46
379 +1 * NZSC cap index +13.48 at 5,265.63
353 +1 * NZMC cap index +15.34 at 2,008.321
391 +1 * Volume NZ$72.5 million. Futures +8 at 1,305
796 +11 * Other movers - +25 +17
The New Zealand share market swam against rising interest rates to power 1.12 percent ahead on Tuesday, leaving the Top 40 index at a record closing high.
It finished up 28.35 at 2,570.46, just a few pips off its session high of 2,570.92. Volume was a healthy $72.5 million.
Brokers were scratching their heads about why the market was able to rise against the sharp lift in short-term rates and some expect a correction after the recent big run.
"I can't work it out," said Doyle Paterson Brown's Philip Solarz.
The most plausible reason appeared to be heightened expectations for a greater easing in monetary policy, he said.
Foreign buyers were buying liquid stocks in anticipation of the easing so there had been little discrimination in favour of exporters despite the New Zealand dollar's sharp fall, he said.
Lead stock Telecom rose to an all-time high of $8.01 before coming off to $7.95, up 10 cents, and still a closing high. All the other top five stocks rose just one cent.
Newspaper stocks Wilson & Horton and Independent Newspapers fared well, rising 20 and 10 cents respectively.
Of those exposed to the New Zealand dollar, fishing company Sanford jumped 25 cents to $2.90 and energy companies Cultus, up 18 to $4.07 and Fletcher Energy, up 19 to $5.26, were the standouts.

"A lower kiwi and higher rates, you might argue, is slightly negative for Telecom," said John Rattray, director of equities at Ord Minnett. "But they seem to have this 'bellwether' status which seems to keep them in the fore even when you get factors like that that might work against them."
He agreed there was a view interest rates would trend down as the RBNZ sights easier monetary conditions later in the year.

Telecom's strength took brokers by surprise, particularly in light of the sluggish New Zealand economy, which has yet to show signs of recovering from its current trough and has been putting corporate earnings under pressure.

"Maybe they're picking a sharp upturn, but I don't think any of the economic forecasters have suddenly come to that view. I think if anything there's concern that this downturn will be more prolonged," said Cavill White's Don Turkington.
